title: Ridgeline Home Improvement Financing Training Note: Payment Tenure and the Late Fee
content:
*Training note for the financing care desk, Ridgeline Home Improvement Financing.*

**The rule.** A late fee on a Ridgeline Home Improvement Financing account whose plan carries no promotion (a fixed-rate or low-payment plan) is multiplied by the tenure share for the borrower's record, counting the whole scheduled payments covered by scheduled-payment entries net of returned payments: at least the long-tenure count of 36 takes the long-tenure share of 90%; at least the mid-tenure count of 24 but under the long-tenure count of 36 takes the mid-tenure share of 95%; fewer leaves the figure whole.

**Q. How are whole scheduled payments covered counted?**
A. Take the money posted on the account as scheduled-payment entries, subtract the money of payments returned unpaid, divide by the scheduled payment, and round down to a whole number. The scheduled payment is the plan's payment factor per 1,000.00 times the financed amount, rounded to the cent, never below the plan's minimum monthly payment.

**Q. What share applies at each count?**

| Whole scheduled payments covered | Late fee multiplied by |
|---|---|
| 36 or more | 90% |
| 24 to 35 | 95% |
| 23 or fewer | 100% (left whole) |

**Q. What about a count exactly on a line?**
A. 36 takes 90% and 35 takes 95%; 24 takes 95% and 23 leaves the figure whole.

**Q. When is the late fee rounded?**
A. The share multiplies the figure before rounding; the late fee is rounded to the cent only as the final figure, to the nearest cent, an exact half cent rounding up.

**Q. Worked example (hypothetical).** Scheduled payment 200.00; scheduled-payment entries total 5100.00 and one returned payment of 200.00: 4900.00 divided by 200.00 is 24.5, rounded down to 24, so a late fee figure of 20.00 becomes 19.00.
